name: Hennesy, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the geofence warrant violated the Minnesota Constitution's particularity requirement, but geofence warrants are not per se unconstitutional and probable cause existed.

name: Hudson, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court should have stayed the case pending the Supreme Court's decision in Chatrie, but acknowledged the remand mitigates this concern.

name: McKeig, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the court should have waited for the Supreme Court's guidance in Chatrie and that the majority failed to establish an adequate and independent state ground for its decision.

name: Moore, III, J.
description: Dissented, joined in the dissent of Justice McKeig.

name: Gaïtas, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Moore, III, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the punishment for unemployment benefit misrepresentation is not grossly disproportional to the offense and therefore does not violate the Excessive Fines Clauses.

name: Hennesy, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that courts must consider a person's ability to pay a fine when analyzing claims under the Excessive Fines Clause and that the case should be remanded to develop an evidentiary record on Thigpen's ability to pay.

name: Procaccini, Justice
description: Dissented, joined Justice Hennesy's dissent regarding the Minnesota Constitution's Excessive Fines Clause requiring consideration of an individual's ability to pay and that remand is appropriate.

name: HUDSON, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the 2024 amendment to the attorney fee cap does not apply retroactively, the Workers' Compensation Court of Appeals did not err in denying excess fees, and the statutory fee cap does not violate the Contracts Clause.

name: PROCACCINI, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Procaccini, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Minnesota Statutes section 253D.20 establishes a waivable right to counsel for civilly committed persons, provided the waiver is knowing and intelligent.

name: Moore, III, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the right to counsel in civil commitment cases is non-waivable, citing concerns about practical effects, potential constitutional issues, and legislative intent.

name: Hennesy, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Gaïtas, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: FRANCIS J. CONNOLLY
description: Concurred, argued that a suspended law license means a candidate is not "learned in the law" as constitutionally required, rendering them ineligible for judicial office.

name: LESLIE E. BEIERS
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: JOHN H. GUTHMANN
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: TIMOTHY J. MCMANUS
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: LAURIE J. MILLER
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HUDSON, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the recall petition failed to allege malfeasance because Jacobs' alleged conduct did not violate a substantive legal standard and she was not acting in her official capacity.

name: HENNESY, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Anne K. McKeig
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PROCACCINI, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: CADISH, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Stadium Referendum violated the Nevada Constitution's full-text requirement and had an inadequate description of effect, thus affirming the district court's injunction.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HERNDON, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PARRAGUIRRE, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: BELL, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Stadium Referendum satisfied the full-text requirement by reprinting only the sections voters were asked to disapprove and that its description of effect was adequate within the word limit, therefore the district court's judgment should be reversed.

name: LEE, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the petition's description of effect was inadequate but disagreed that it violated the full-text requirement, joining the dissent on the latter point.

name: MOORE, III, Justice
description: Concurred with the majority opinion, affirming the Governor's authority and the constitutionality of the Act.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, but argued that prolonged executive emergency orders raise serious concerns requiring legislative consideration and that more legislative participation would strengthen the Act's constitutional standing.

name: PROCACCINI, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: HUDSON, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that taxpayer standing exists only when the central dispute involves alleged unlawful disbursements of public funds, not when expenditures are incidental to implementing a substantive law.

name: HENNESY, J.J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GAÏTAS, J.J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: ANDERSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that when the purpose of a public charity is to provide affordable housing, the exclusive residential occupancy of the property by its clients fulfills the constitutional requirement for tax exemption.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule does not extend to searches and arrests based on quashed warrants that appear active due to clerical errors by court administration, as applying the exclusionary rule in such cases deters unlawful government conduct and promotes judicial fairness.

name: PROCACCINI, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Chutich, J.
description: Concurred, argued that racial imbalances alone are not sufficient to establish a violation of the Education Clause; plaintiffs must prove racial imbalances are a substantial factor in causing an inadequate education.

name: Hudson, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that de facto segregation in public schools is sufficient, standing alone, to establish a violation of the Education Clause, as it undermines the purpose of providing an adequate education and has historical state entanglement.

name: Procaccini, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: THISSEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the district court's exclusion of the public from the courtroom during the COVID-19 pandemic was a closure implicating the defendant's public trial right, and the record was insufficient to determine if the right was violated, necessitating a remand for further findings on alternatives to closure.

name: McKEIG, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the district court's findings were sufficient to conclude that Bell's public trial right was not violated, given the unprecedented circumstances of the COVID-19 pandemic and the court's adherence to public health guidelines.

name: GILDEA, Chief Justice
description: Dissented, joined Justice McKeig's opinion that the district court's findings were sufficient and the majority was "moving the goalposts" by requiring more.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the unconstitutional section 4.08 was integral to the proposed charter amendment's efficacy and strength, and therefore not severable, affirming the district court's decision.

name: THISSEN, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the three valid sections of the proposed charter amendment were severable and stood on their own, and the city council should have been required to place them on the ballot, respecting the constitutional right of residents to govern themselves.

name: THISSEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the Minnesota Constitution requires an affirmative act to restore voting rights, not automatic restoration upon release, and the statute is constitutional under rational basis review.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the constitutional phrase "unless restored to civil rights" does not mean automatic restoration upon release, and the statute is constitutional, but disagreed with the majority's equal protection analysis method.

name: GILDEA, Chief Justice
description: Concurred with Justice Anderson's opinion.

name: HUDSON, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the statute creates a racial classification in practice with a disparate impact on people of color and fails under heightened rational basis review, violating equal protection.

name: ANDERSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the tax court erred in its application of the "seminary of learning" standard, finding that Rainbow presented uncontroverted evidence of its educational nature, general curriculum, and comprehensive teaching, thus qualifying for tax exemption.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the State presented sufficient evidence for conviction and that the mandatory life sentence for a 21-year-old for first-degree premeditated murder is not unconstitutionally cruel.

name: CHUTICH, Justice
description: Concurred that the State presented sufficient evidence but dissented on the sentencing issue, arguing that a mandatory life sentence without parole for a 21-year-old may be unconstitutionally cruel given brain science, and proposed individualized sentencing hearings for youthful offenders.

name: THISSEN, Justice
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, joining Justice Chutich's opinion regarding the sentencing issue.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the unanimity requirement for pardons is constitutional as the pardon power is not solely the governor's and the chief justice's participation is explicitly allowed.

name: Lorie Gildea
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: HUDSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that expanding a traffic stop to investigate a non-criminal pretrial release violation is an unlawful seizure under the Minnesota Constitution, as it requires reasonable articulable suspicion of criminal activity.

name: MOORE, III, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that while the decision is legally sound, it creates difficulties for law enforcement in enforcing pretrial release conditions related to public safety.

name: McKEIG, Justice
description: Concurred with Justice Moore's opinion.

name: THISSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the UMDDA provides a right to final disposition only when charges remain pending, and Mikell's constitutional speedy trial right was not violated.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the plain language of the UMDDA unambiguously requires the State to bring untried charges to trial within 6 months following a request, and the court erred by reading an exception into the statute.
